title: Checkpointed streaming migration playbook for SDKs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: PRD: Provide a vendor-guided migration path for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs to support checkpointed streaming cursors and compatibility guarantees. Background: multiple customers running long-lived streaming flows (token deltas, realtime embeddings flows, and incremental evals) reported need for resumability across sdk updates and transient failures. Current SDKs expose streaming iterators but lack a standardized opaque checkpoint token and a compatibility matrix for format evolution. Goal: define API surfaces, wire protocol expectations, documented migration playbook, and acceptance tests so SDK teams can implement with minimal runtime breakage. Non-goals: full wire-level version negotiation for custom on-prem deployments (handled by Private runtime docs), and automatic client-side state reconciliation for divergent message schemas.
acceptance_criteria: Python/TS/Go SDKs expose a stable 'Checkpoint' token returned by streaming endpoints that is opaque and base64-encoded
Clients can provide the Checkpoint to resume a stream and receive identical logical events (idempotent semantics) for any events after the checkpoint
Server-side behavior: replay from a checkpoint preserves order and delivers the same event ids; deduplication is applied for previously seen ids
Backward compatibility: SDK vNext can both consume vPrev checkpoints and emit vPrev-compatible checkpoints when a compatibility flag is set
End-to-end automated tests (integration) exist in CI that validate resume-after-failure scenarios for each SDK and platform matrix (linux/macos/windows for desktop runtimes where relevant)
Documentation: migration guide published in SDK docs with examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go, plus a compatibility table per release
Rollout plan: canary rollout to 5% of hosted customers, with quantitative metrics (resume-success-rate, duplicate-event-rate, median-lag) tracked in Console dashboards before full rollout
notes: Design decision: use opaque checkpoint token to avoid coupling SDK parsing to server internals; server keeps mapping to KV cache entries
Trade-off: checkpoint size vs fidelity — decided on compact token with server-side tombstone window of 24h to bound replay cost
Interoperability: include a short version-byte in token to allow forward-compatible parsing in advanced cases
Fallback strategy: clients without resume support will get a documented deprecation warning but not be immediately broken; server will maintain short replay window
Performance consideration: replay can be slightly higher tail-cost; will gate heavy replays behind autoscaling and request-priority controls
